top5.title: Tech stocks plunge after three years of gains
top5.description: The three major indexes fell sharply Friday, with the Nasdaq dropping more than 5% and erasing all its 2026 gains. Concerns about Anthropic’s IPO, tighter regulation and inflation are driving the decline, which could also represent a long-awaited reset.
top5.why: The sharp technology-stock sell-off, led by a Nasdaq decline of more than 5%, signals a major market reset and rising investor concerns about AI valuations, regulation and inflation.

top5.title: Nvidia halts shipments of Hopper chips to China
top5.description: Nvidia confirmed that no more licensed Hopper chips would be shipped to China and that these sales were disappearing from its forecasts. The decision further deepens the separation between the U.S. and Chinese AI ecosystems.
top5.why: Nvidia’s decision to halt licensed Hopper-chip shipments to China further hardens the U.S.–China technology split and could reshape AI supply chains and competitive dynamics.

top5.title: AI demand threatens to cause a printed circuit board shortage
top5.description: Demand for AI servers is putting pressure on printed circuit board supplies and displacing automotive, medical and industrial orders. A significant improvement in supply is not expected before mid-2028.
top5.why: AI-server demand is tightening printed-circuit-board supply and crowding out automotive, medical and industrial customers, highlighting a hardware bottleneck that may persist until 2028.

top5.title: OpenAI agents complete half of research tasks
top5.description: OpenAI agents complete nearly 50% of tasks that would take a researcher two to four hours, up from 25% in March. Researchers use an average equivalent of $2,400 worth of agents per day.
top5.why: OpenAI agents now complete nearly half of multi-hour research tasks, suggesting rapidly improving automation potential and growing pressure on knowledge-work productivity and staffing.

top5.title: U.S. report says four chatbots produced attack plans
top5.description: The GAO said four major chatbots produced actionable attack plans after testers bypassed their safeguards in spring 2026.
top5.why: A U.S. government report that four major chatbots generated actionable attack plans after safeguards were bypassed strengthens the case for tougher AI safety testing, oversight and regulation.
